scenes.heading: What covalent bonds are
scenes.narration: A covalent bond is one of the main ways that atoms attach to each other. You will find these bonds inside almost every molecule that makes up living things around you.

scenes.heading: Electrons in the middle
scenes.narration: In a covalent bond the two atoms share a pair of electrons. Neither atom hands its electron over completely, so the pair sits in the region between the two nuclei instead.

scenes.heading: Counting the outer shell
scenes.narration: Because the shared pair belongs to both partners at once, each atom can count those electrons toward its own outer shell, which is how the octet requirement gets satisfied here.

scenes.heading: Single double and triple
scenes.narration: Atoms can share more than one pair. Sharing one pair gives a single bond, two shared pairs give a double bond, and three shared pairs give the triple bond found in nitrogen gas.

scenes.heading: Covalent bonds recap
scenes.narration: So a covalent bond means two atoms sharing one or more electron pairs, each counting the shared electrons in its own outer shell, as you see in hydrogen gas, water and methane.

points: Shared pairs fill the outer shell
